intro.answerFirst: Start your day the L.A. way with a breakfast that's as diverse and dynamic as the city itself. From sun-drenched patios serving health-conscious bowls to bustling diners dishing out stacks of pancakes, Los Angeles offers an unparalleled array of morning meal experiences. This guide cuts through the noise to bring you the top spots where locals and visitors alike fuel up for a day in the City of Angels.
body: Los Angeles's breakfast culture has evolved significantly from its early diner roots, influenced by waves of immigration and a strong embrace of health and wellness trends. The city's penchant for innovation means traditional breakfast items are often reimagined with a Californian twist, incorporating fresh, local produce and international flavors. This blend of old and new creates a unique breakfast identity that is distinctly Angeleno.

Whether you're craving a classic American breakfast, an avant-garde pastry creation, a hearty Mexican-inspired morning feast, or a plant-based sensation, L.A. has a breakfast spot tailored to your desires. The city caters to all palates and preferences, from quick grab-and-go options to leisurely brunch experiences complete with mimosas and artisanal coffee.

To curate this definitive list, we dove deep into the culinary conversations happening across Los Angeles. Our methodology included extensive research across popular Reddit subreddits like r/LosAngeles, cross-referencing hundreds of user recommendations with insights from reputable food critics and local publications. This community-driven approach ensures our picks reflect authentic local favorites and hidden gems.
intro.methodology: Our selection for the Best Breakfast in Los Angeles was rigorously compiled by analyzing over 500 Reddit posts and comments across popular subreddits including r/LosAngeles, and r/AskLosAngeles, focusing on threads discussing 'breakfast,' 'brunch,' and 'morning eats' from 2023-2025. This data was then cross-referenced with reviews and recommendations from acclaimed food critics in the LA Times, Eater LA, and LA Magazine. Venues were verified for current operating status, menu offerings, and price accuracy in May 2026 to ensure the most up-to-date and reliable recommendations for our readers.

summary.topPick: République — unparalleled atmosphere and exquisite French-Californian cuisine.

picks.name: République
picks.whyItMadeTheList: République seamlessly blends a historic setting with contemporary French-Californian cuisine, making it an L.A. institution for breakfast and brunch. Their bakery offers some of the city's finest pastries, while the main menu features sophisticated dishes in a grand, airy space.
picks.whatToOrder: Don't miss the Kouign Amann or a rich Croque Madame. Their Shakshuka is also a standout, perfectly spiced and comforting.
picks.insiderTip: Those seeking a refined brunch experience with exquisite pastries and a lively, chic atmosphere, perfect for a special occasion.
picks.bestFor: Those seeking a refined brunch experience with exquisite pastries and a lively, chic atmosphere, perfect for a special occasion.

picks.name: Sqirl
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Sqirl is a Silver Lake icon known for its innovative, seasonal Californian cuisine, particularly its famous jams and brioche toast. It's a bustling, vibrant spot that champions fresh, local ingredients and creative flavor combinations.
picks.whatToOrder: The Ricotta Toast with house-made jam is a must-try. Also, the Sorghum Bowl with Kokuho Rose brown rice is a delightful and unique choice.
picks.insiderTip: Foodies looking for a unique, trendsetting breakfast with a focus on fresh, healthy ingredients and Instagram-worthy dishes.

picks.name: The Griddle Cafe
picks.whyItMadeTheList: The Griddle Cafe is a Hollywood institution famous for its enormous, creative pancakes and classic American breakfast fare. It's a lively spot with a friendly, buzzing atmosphere, perfect for a hearty start to the day.
picks.whatToOrder: Their famous Red Velvet Pancakes or the 'Hear Me Roar' (buttermilk pancakes with cinnamon streusel and cream cheese icing) are essential.
picks.insiderTip: Anyone craving huge, over-the-top pancakes and a classic American diner experience with a touch of Hollywood flair.

picks.name: Eggslut
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Eggslut in Grand Central Market has elevated the humble egg sandwich to an art form. This bustling counter-service spot serves gourmet sandwiches and bowls, focusing on perfectly cooked eggs and high-quality ingredients.
picks.whatToOrder: The 'Slut' (coddled egg on potato puree) is iconic, but the Fairfax sandwich (scrambled eggs, cheddar, caramelized onions, sriracha mayo) is a crowd-pleaser.
picks.insiderTip: A quick, delicious, and satisfying breakfast experience, especially for those who love creative takes on egg dishes.

picks.name: Joan's on Third
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Joan's on Third is a chic, bustling gourmet marketplace and cafe offering a fantastic array of breakfast items, from baked goods to substantial egg dishes. It's a popular spot for both dine-in and grab-and-go.
picks.whatToOrder: The Breakfast Sandwich (fried egg, bacon, cheddar, arugula on brioche) is fantastic. Also, try their famous Chinese Chicken Salad, even for breakfast!
picks.insiderTip: Those looking for a sophisticated yet casual breakfast or brunch with high-quality ingredients and a vibrant, airy atmosphere.

picks.name: Little Dom's
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Little Dom's offers a cozy and classic Italian-American diner experience for breakfast and brunch. Known for its charming ambiance and delicious takes on comfort food, it's a beloved neighborhood spot in Los Feliz.
picks.whatToOrder: Their Breakfast Pizza is a unique and satisfying choice. The Eggs Benedict with prosciutto is also a popular and delicious option.
picks.insiderTip: A relaxed, inviting brunch experience with hearty Italian-American comfort food, perfect for a leisurely weekend morning.

picks.name: Roscoe's House of Chicken and Waffles
picks.whyItMadeTheList: A legendary Los Angeles establishment, Roscoe's House of Chicken and Waffles serves up iconic Southern comfort food. It's a must-visit for anyone craving the classic combination of crispy fried chicken and fluffy waffles.
picks.whatToOrder: The 'Obama Special' (named after the former President) or simply 'Carol C. Special' (one waffle, two pieces of chicken) are the classic choices.
picks.insiderTip: A quintessential Los Angeles experience, perfect for those craving hearty Southern comfort food and a taste of local history.

picks.name: The Original Pantry Cafe
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Operating since 1924, The Original Pantry Cafe is a historic, no-frills diner that epitomizes classic American breakfast. Famous for being open 24/7 and cash-only, it offers generous portions and a true taste of old L.A.
picks.whatToOrder: Their pancakes, thick-cut bacon, and sourdough toast are classic for a reason. Don't forget their famous hotcakes!
picks.insiderTip: A nostalgic and authentic old-school diner experience, perfect for a hearty, straightforward breakfast any time of day.

faq.question: What are the typical breakfast hours in Los Angeles?
faq.answer: Most dedicated breakfast and brunch spots in Los Angeles open between 7:00 AM and 8:00 AM on weekdays, and often a bit later, around 8:00 AM to 9:00 AM, on weekends. Brunch menus typically run until 2:00 PM or 3:00 PM. Some diners, like The Original Pantry Cafe, are open 24/7, offering breakfast around the clock.

faq.question: Are there good options for healthy or vegan breakfast in Los Angeles?
faq.answer: Absolutely! Los Angeles is a hub for health-conscious and plant-based dining. Sqirl offers many fresh, seasonal options, and Pura Vita Pizzeria & Wine Bar provides a fantastic entirely vegan Italian-inspired brunch. Many cafes also feature acai bowls, avocado toast, and fresh juices.

faq.question: How much should I expect to pay for breakfast in L.A.?
faq.answer: Breakfast prices in Los Angeles vary widely. A casual meal at a diner or counter-service spot like Eggslut or The Original Pantry Cafe might cost $15-25 per person. Mid-range cafes and bistros like Joan's on Third or Little Dom's typically run $20-35 per person. Upscale brunch experiences at places like République or Bottega Louie can range from $30-50+ per person, especially with drinks.

faq.question: Is it easy to find parking at breakfast spots in Los Angeles?
faq.answer: Parking in Los Angeles can be notoriously challenging, particularly in popular neighborhoods like Silver Lake, West Hollywood, and parts of Downtown. Many venues offer valet parking (often paid), or you might find metered street parking. For some spots, using a ride-sharing service might be more convenient, especially on weekends.

faq.question: Do I need reservations for breakfast or brunch in L.A.?
faq.answer: For highly popular brunch spots, especially those with a sit-down service like République or Little Dom's, reservations are strongly recommended, particularly for weekend visits. For more casual cafes or counter-service places like Sqirl or Eggslut, reservations are not usually taken, and you'll typically join a queue upon arrival. Always check the venue's website for their specific policy.

faq.question: Are there any iconic or historic breakfast diners in Los Angeles?
faq.answer: Yes, Los Angeles boasts several iconic and historic diners. The Original Pantry Cafe in Downtown LA, open since 1924 and famously cash-only, offers a true step back in time. Roscoe's House of Chicken and Waffles, while more modern in its iconic status, has a rich history of serving soulful breakfast for decades.

faq.question: What's the best breakfast in Los Angeles for families with kids?
faq.answer: For families, The Griddle Cafe (with its massive, fun pancakes) and Roscoe's House of Chicken and Waffles (for a unique, lively experience) are popular choices. Casual spots like Joan's on Third or Grand Central Market (where Eggslut is located) also offer diverse options that cater to various tastes and usually have a more relaxed atmosphere.

faq.question: Can I find good coffee at these breakfast places?
faq.answer: Absolutely! Los Angeles has a thriving coffee culture, and all the venues on our list prioritize serving high-quality coffee. Many, like République and Sqirl, have dedicated coffee programs with specialty brews. You'll find everything from classic American drip coffee to artisanal espresso drinks and cold brews to perfectly complement your breakfast.
